reference.source: Rook's Textbook of Dermatology / Fitzpatrick's Dermatology
clinicalPearls: Presents with severe, treatment-resistant stomatitis and a polymorphous cutaneous eruption that can mimic pemphigus, pemphigoid, erythema multiforme, or lichen planus
Almost always associated with an underlying neoplasm, most often lymphoproliferative (non-Hodgkin lymphoma, chronic lymphocytic leukaemia, Castleman disease) or thymoma
Intractable painful mucositis, particularly of the lips and oral cavity, is a hallmark and often the presenting feature
Autoantibodies target plakin proteins, characteristically envoplakin and periplakin, as well as desmogleins and other desmosomal and hemidesmosomal antigens
Bronchiolitis obliterans from respiratory epithelial involvement is a feared complication and a leading cause of death
Direct immunofluorescence shows intercellular IgG/C3 with variable basement-membrane-zone deposition; indirect immunofluorescence on rat bladder epithelium is a supportive screening test
Management centres on treating the underlying tumour alongside immunosuppression, though skin disease is often refractory
reference.pathophysiology: Paraneoplastic pemphigus is an autoimmune blistering disease arising in the context of neoplasia, especially lymphoproliferative disorders. Tumour-related immune dysregulation drives production of autoantibodies against a broad panel of antigens, characteristically the plakin family proteins envoplakin and periplakin, together with desmogleins and other desmosomal and hemidesmosomal components. This wide antigen targeting explains the polymorphous mucocutaneous picture, combining intraepidermal acantholysis with interface (lichenoid) inflammation. Both humoral and cell-mediated mechanisms contribute, and antibody or cytotoxic attack on respiratory epithelium can produce bronchiolitis obliterans, contributing to high mortality.
additionalInvestigations: Skin and mucosal biopsy showing combined acantholysis and interface dermatitis
Direct immunofluorescence for intercellular and basement-membrane-zone immune deposits
Indirect immunofluorescence including rat bladder epithelium substrate
Immunoblot or immunoprecipitation for anti-envoplakin/periplakin and other plakin antibodies
Imaging (CT of chest, abdomen, pelvis) and haematological workup to identify an occult neoplasm
Pulmonary function tests to detect airflow obstruction from bronchiolitis obliterans
redFlags: Progressive dyspnoea or airflow obstruction suggesting bronchiolitis obliterans
Newly diagnosed or occult lymphoproliferative malignancy requiring urgent oncological input
Severe intractable mucositis compromising nutrition, hydration, and the airway
Widespread erosions with sepsis risk and failure of standard immunosuppression
reference.prognosis: Prognosis is generally poor, with high mortality driven by the underlying malignancy, sepsis, and respiratory failure from bronchiolitis obliterans; skin disease may improve if a benign tumour is fully removed but often remains refractory.
pitfalls: Attributing severe stomatitis to aphthous ulceration or infection and missing an underlying malignancy
Not screening for an occult neoplasm once the diagnosis is suspected
Overlooking early respiratory symptoms that herald bronchiolitis obliterans
Expecting a standard pemphigus response to immunosuppression when the disease is characteristically treatment-resistant
management: Treatment of the underlying neoplasm, including surgical removal of a localised tumour such as Castleman disease or thymoma, or chemotherapy for lymphoproliferative disease
Immunosuppression with systemic corticosteroids combined with steroid-sparing agents, notably rituximab, with adjuncts such as intravenous immunoglobulin, ciclosporin, azathioprine or mycophenolate
Intensive mucocutaneous care with meticulous wound management, analgesia for stomatitis, and prevention and prompt treatment of secondary infection and sepsis
Pulmonary function monitoring for bronchiolitis obliterans, a leading cause of death, with respiratory support as needed
Ophthalmological assessment and management of ocular mucosal involvement
Coordinated dermatology and haematology or oncology multidisciplinary management, with recognition of the generally poor prognosis
